summary: Three paragraph-specific gaps justify a small retrieval pass: width-aware parametrization theory, direct prior work on how grokking depends on model width/scale, and statistical methodology for the cluster bootstrap and censored-delay analysis.
missing_literatures: width-aware parametrization and hyperparameter transfer under Adam (muP / Tensor Programs)
empirical studies of how grokking time depends on model width, size, or weight decay
cluster bootstrap and right-censored (survival / Tobit) regression

rewrite_targets.reason: The evaluated model's central design element is a width-dependent multiplier meant to equalize the effective step size under Adam-type updates, and the Discussion argues this could mask or create a width slope. The paragraph supports this only with a reinforcement-learning normalization paper and a dynamical-richness measurement paper; the standard width-aware parametrization literature that motivates exactly this construction is not cited.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Parametrization and optimizer scale: ... width-dependent multipliers on hidden and output layers
search_topics: maximal update parametrization feature learning in infinite-width networks
hyperparameter transfer across width (muP, Tensor Programs V)
Adam learning-rate scaling with width / parametrization-dependent effective step size

rewrite_targets.reason: The paper's question is how grokking delay depends on model width, yet no cited work is positioned as having measured delay versus width or model size. Readers will expect the paper to say what earlier empirical grokking studies (modular arithmetic, varying width, weight decay, training fraction, or initialization scale) already found, and the 'Relation to this work' paragraph claims novelty of scope without this positioning. The capacity-based reading in the model-size paragraph is also supported only by general memorization and double-descent papers.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: How the delay depends on model size is a more practical question ... a capacity-based reading predicts that wider models memorize sooner
search_topics: grokking modular arithmetic dependence on model width and weight decay
grokking time scaling with model size or dataset size
grokking and initialization scale or effective learning rate

rewrite_targets.reason: The test statistic relies on a seed-cluster percentile bootstrap, and delays right-censored at the step limit are entered at the cap. The Discussion recommends analyzing delays as censored data. None of this methodology is cited, so the design choices and the proposed remedy are unsupported by methodological references.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Test statistic and decision rule ... cluster bootstrap over seeds; 'analyze delays as censored data instead of imputing the cap'
search_topics: regression with right-censored outcomes (Tobit / accelerated failure time)
bias from imputing censored values at a cap
